title: Production Guardian — metrics proxy API
description: Schemas for GET /proxy/metrics, /proxy/alerts and /proxy/health. Owner: Dev A. See proxy-api.md.

Timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC, Z-suffixed. Sub-second digits optional: JS toISOString() emits milliseconds, Python isoformat() microseconds. Same pattern as healthscan.schema.json.

NullableNumber.description: null means IRIS reported no series for this metric; 0 means IRIS measured zero. Never conflate them — see proxy-api.md §1.1.

NullableCount.description: Cumulative count. null means the metric family was absent, not zero.

host.description: Config item name from the IRIS `host` label. Display name, so it contains spaces ('Lab Router'). The join key through to Finding.host — NOT `name`, see proxy-api.md Q9.

type.description: Normalized host type. IRIS reports processes as 'actor'; the proxy maps actor -> process. 'unknown' when IRIS emitted no avg_* series for the host, which is the only place the hosttype label rides — a real value, not a defect.

status.description: The IRIS `status` label, passed through. 'Unknown' when no iris_interop_hosts line was emitted for this host. There is no 'Active' and no 'Warning'. Enumerated for validation; consumers must still render unrecognized values neutrally rather than failing.

isFramework.description: True for IRIS's own plumbing (Ens.*, EnsLib.*, and the bare 'ActivityReporter' spelling). A flag rather than a filter: dropping these at the proxy would hide them from the consumer with no way to ask why. 11 of 15 hosts in samples/metrics-dump.txt are framework.

queued.description: Per-host queue depth. null on every host today: iris_interop_queued carries no host label, so the value is not in /api/monitor/metrics at all. The per-production total is _meta.productionQueued. 0 is the contract-conformant placeholder — see proxy-api.md §6.1, issue #12.

messages.description: Cumulative messages processed since production start.

messagesPerSec.description: Throughput over the IRIS sampling window.

errored.description: Cumulative errored messages. null on every host today: iris_interop_messages_errored carries no host label either, and unlike queued no per-production total is published. See proxy-api.md Q8 and §6.3. Named `errored` to match the ratified healthscan contract, not `messagesErrored` — §6.2 is a request for a decision.

avgProcessingTime.description: SECONDS. Aggregated across message types, weighted by iris_interop_sample_count — IRIS emits one series per (host, messagetype). null when the host has processed nothing since stats were enabled.

lastActivity.description: Derived as polledAt minus lastActivityElapsedSeconds, so accuracy is bounded by poll timing — treat as +/-10s. null when IRIS emitted no last_activity line, rather than reading as 'active just now'.

lastActivityElapsedSeconds.description: Seconds since last activity as iris_interop_last_activity holds it — ELAPSED SECONDS, not an epoch timestamp. This is the measurement; prefer it over lastActivity for stalled_host.

ProxyAlert.description: One /api/monitor/alerts entry, forwarded upstream-shaped. additionalProperties stays open deliberately: the alerts payload is pinned by a single capture obtained on a first-ever read, so an unfamiliar key must not fail validation.

time.description: As IRIS emits it. Not pattern-constrained: this is upstream's format, not ours.

severity.description: A NUMERIC STRING ('2'), matching the level column in alerts.log — not a word. Mapping it to info/warning/critical is the consumer's decision, see proxy-api.md §6.2.

observedAt.description: The proxy's addition: the poll that observed this alert. IRIS alert bodies carry no unique id, so this is what distinguishes two identical repeated messages.

MetricsMeta.description: Diagnostics, not payload. Nothing here should feed a finding.

polledAt.description: When the proxy sampled IRIS. null while warming. The only staleness signal — there is no X-Proxy-State header.

productionQueued.description: iris_interop_queued: the per-PRODUCTION total. The only real queue number available from /api/monitor/metrics.

absentFamilies.description: Tracked metric families IRIS did not emit. A family listed here is 'unmeasurable on this instance', NOT zero.

shape.description: How the upstream payload was interpreted. Anything other than array/empty/wrapped:* means a zero count is a mapping gap, not a healthy production. Open string: `wrapped:<key>` and `unrecognized-<type>` are parameterized.

count.description: Alerts in the accumulating buffer — NOT the last poll's count.

newInLastPoll.description: The last poll's own count. 0 is the normal steady state under consume-on-read.

droppedCount.description: Alerts evicted from the 500-entry buffer. Non-zero means the list is no longer complete, and the data is unrecoverable.

suspectShapeMismatch.description: True when metrics saw unread alerts the last alerts poll did not return. A hint toward a mapping problem, not a verdict.

raw.description: The unrecognized payload, kept rather than discarded. Any type.

MetricsResponse.description: GET /proxy/metrics. Always 200, including during the startup window — see the warming note below and proxy-api.md §4.

hosts.description: Stable alphabetical order by host. Empty while warming, or when the production is stopped.

systemAlertsNew.description: iris_system_alerts_new. Consume-on-read, so it reads 0 almost always on a proxy that polls alerts.

systemAlertsLog.description: iris_system_alerts_log. Durable count from alerts.log; does not reset on read.

warming.description: Present and true ONLY before the first poll completes; absent afterwards. 200 rather than 503 deliberately: a 503 read to the engine as 'proxy is down' and produced a spurious finding on every restart (issue #10).

AlertsResponse.description: GET /proxy/alerts. `alerts` is cumulative since proxy start, not per-poll — /api/monitor/alerts is consume-on-read and the proxy's own poll is what clears it from IRIS.

HealthResponse.description: GET /proxy/health. The endpoint a smoke test should assert on: 'ok' means a poll completed AND described a production, which 'a poll succeeded' alone did not.

status.description: 'reachable, but no interop metrics' is the %SYS-namespace case: HTTP 200, hundreds of real metric lines, not one iris_interop_* family. Indistinguishable from a stopped production without this.

hint.description: Present only on 'reachable, but no interop metrics'. Names the likely cause, usually a wrong IRIS_BASE_PATH.
